children: to provide cloud infrastructure and software to support CPU growth reinforces just how important CPUs have become to artificial intelligence, GF Securities said.
“The deal is expected to be on Nvidia’s
Vera CPUs, which Akamai previously disclosed as its planned platform for agentic workloads,” GF Securities analyst Henry Huang wrote in a note to clients.
Akamai is expected to invest roughly $5.5B in capex, including $1.7B in 2026 for components such as DRAM.

“The deployment should also boost eSSD demand as vector databases, KV‑cache, and context storage requirements increase,” Huang added. “Overall, we expect stronger structural CPU demand and expect [a] 2030 server CPU [total addressable market] of $215 billion. AMD
, ABF substrates, advanced packaging, and Lenovo positioned as key beneficiaries.”

The deal is worth $11.6B over seven years and could be worth as much as $20B if certain conditions are met. As part of the deal, Akamai gave warrants to Anthropic that represent 7.7M shares of its Series B preferred stock that convert to roughly 5% of Akamai's common stock outstanding, at an exercise price of $111.33 per share of common stock. Part of the warrant representing 2% of Akamai's shares is expected to vest in connection with the agreement, Akamai added.
Akamai shares rose 19% in premarket trading on Friday following news of the deal.

title: Akamai's deal with Anthropic should boost CPU demand, GF says
